phase1.explanation:
🦀 **Traits define shared behavior across types.**

**Common standard traits:**

| Trait | What it does |
|-------|--------------|
| `Debug` | Format with `{:?}` |
| `Display` | Format with `{}` |
| `PartialEq` | Equality (`==`, `!=`) |
| `Eq` | Full equality |
| `PartialOrd` | Partial ordering (`<`, `>`) |
| `Ord` | Full ordering |
| `Clone` | Explicit clone |
| `Default` | Default value |
| `Copy` | Implicit copy |

**Rust-chan says:**
"Standard library traits are powerful. Implement them to get useful functionality for free."

**Trait bounds:**
| Syntax | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `fn f<T: Trait>(x: &T)` | T must implement Trait |
| `fn f(x: &impl Trait)` | Same as above (sugar) |
| `fn f<T: Trait1 + Trait2>(x: &T)` | Multiple bounds |
| `fn f<T>(x: &T) where T: Trait` | Where clause |
